When disabled, EUI relinquishes full control of friendly player nameplates to Blizzard. Use Blizzard's own Nameplate settings (Esc > Options > Nameplates) to control them.
When enabled, BM and MM specs show Focus as the standard power bar instead of a class resource bar.

When enabled, debuff icons keep Blizzard's colored border instead of using the custom border.
When enabled, left-click dragging a window will save its position without needing to hold Shift. Ctrl+drag still does a temporary move.
When enabled, left-click dragging the bag window will move it without needing to hold Shift.
When enabled, nameplates stack vertically instead of overlapping.
When enabled, the extra buttons (Great Vault, M+ Portals, Friends Online, Group Button) and any ungrouped minimap buttons only show while the mouse is over the minimap. The M+ Portals flyout keeps them shown until it closes.
When hovering any action bar set to Mouseover, all Mouseover bars will appear.
When the class resource bar is not shown, this automatically adds the class resource height to the power bar.
When using custom raid sizes, don't count members in hidden groups toward the raid-size breakpoint. For example, if you hide groups 7 and 8, a full 40-man raid is sized as if it were 24-man instead of jumping to the 30-man frame size. Has no effect unless you have custom raid sizes set up.
When you are solo, center the player frame on the party frame instead of anchoring it at the top.
When you join a Group Finder group for a dungeon that has a teleport, shows a small movable popup with the dungeon name and a one-click teleport button. It hides when you enter the dungeon, leave the group, or enter combat.
When you press Escape or Space during a cinematic, the confirmation prompt is automatically accepted.
